name: Cowlitz River (below Mayfield Dam)
blurb: Big, dam-fed, easy river famous for salmon and steelhead — a fast, mellow float.

sections.notes: Busy fishing river — expect drift boats and anglers. Cold, powerful water. Both launches are run by Tacoma Power, which says there is no fee to use them (Blue Creek allows camping up to 3 days, no fires).

putInAccess.sourceName: Tacoma Power: Cowlitz Salmon Hatchery (Barrier Dam Boat Launch)
putInAccess.note: WDFW ramp feature is at the paved lot edge ~30-35 m from the waterline; water end on the gravel shore not resolvable (research/raw/batch4/bd19_g.png). Restrictions: posted hours; heavy fishing traffic
putInAccess.directions: Tacoma Power Barrier Dam Boat Launch below the Cowlitz Salmon Hatchery barrier dam; ramp from the paved lot down the gravel shore.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Tacoma Power — Blue Creek (Cowlitz Trout Hatchery)
takeOutAccess.note: Tacoma Power explicitly confirms free public river access, a boat launch and parking. WDFW publishes this coordinate for the adjacent ADA fishing platforms and explicitly distinguishes those platforms from the Tacoma Power ramp. The agency aerial photo and individual satellite image identify the same hatchery-side facility. This is an approximate access area, not an exact ramp or a choice between unverified nearby ramps.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use Tacoma Power’s signed Blue Creek Boat Launch at 273 Blue Creek Lane, Toledo. The Area marker is the adjacent fishing-platform vicinity; locate the actual ramp from the launch parking, not the marker.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 1). Tacoma Power confirms both launches (Barrier Dam, Blue Creek) are public and free, but it publishes addresses only. WDFW's Barrier Dam ramp feature sits at the ramp head in the lot, about 30-35 m from the water. Blue Creek has no agency ramp feature. Pending until on-ramp agency coordinates are found for both.
